try and imagine a bigger W as an academic
This is a distressingly solid analogy 🐝🍯

Wherein I write about the step beyond Google Zero and imagine the AI information ecosystem collapse:

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/who-really...
You need to pay for news
When Baz Luhrman had the guns say "sword" on the side in Romeo + Juliet, that was the best choice that has been made in any modern adaptation ever.

Beyond the theft, the technology is absolutely there to capture sources for attribution.

That these companies lean toward obscuring sources is telling.

the paywall finding is the part that should terrify publishers. 64% coverage of paywalled content. subscriptions aren't a revenue wall anymore, they're a speed bump for a crawler that attributes the source 1 to 16% of the time

Today in AI plunder:

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/who-really...
you can’t be named this
Watching baseball. The pitcher's name is Kody Funderburk. The batter's name is Coby Mayo. We are not a serious civilization
AI plundering paywalled and unpaywalled work alike

WAR DON'T SEX

CRIMES HIDE CRIMES

Wherein I write about the step beyond Google Zero and imagine the AI information ecosystem collapse:

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/who-really...
genuinely fascinating that we’ve hit a point where the full monetization of the internet and ai bot takeover has led to a majority of people wanting tech minimalism

Huge result here - the idea that social platforms can be defective products that cause harm is going to send shockwaves through an industry that has claimed essentially blanket protection from liability by saying everything is speech
when you’re watching right-wing media consolidation run into the wall of capitalist discipline
This Piketty breakdown of modern politics (four blocs broken across axes of property rights and immigration) seems basically right.

Here’s my interview with Shishir Mehotra, the CEO behind Grammarly’s “expert review” feature which attributed writing advice to people - including me lol - without permission. Or, as you will hear us talk about a lot, compensation. www.theverge.com/podcast/8987...
swiping left or right one someone's profile probably feels incredible if you do it on one of the big chunky knobs on this bad boy
